parsed.doc_summary: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 (as amended by AB 1170, eff. 1/1/2026) regulates tenant application screening fees in California: $30 base cap CPI-adjusted since 1998, availability and refund conditions, itemized receipt, credit report copy.

rules.title: California application screening fee limits
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge an application screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs and never more than $30 per applicant (CPI-adjusted annually since 1998). No fee if no unit is or will soon be available; the landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and offer first-come-first-served screening or a full refund to unselected applicants.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.effective_date_note: Effective date of the AB 1170 amendment (Stats. 2025, Ch. 67); the cap itself dates from earlier versions. The statute does not state a single current CPI-adjusted dollar figure.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants, including guarantors/cosigners.
rules.interaction: Not considered security under § 1950.5; does not preempt rules on deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.conflict_note: The adjusted dollar cap after CPI increases is not stated in the statute text.
